articles.title: The Siang dam and a threatened homeland
articles.description: The Adi community has been protesting against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, saying it threatens their land, livelihoods, and civilisation. The agitation has turned violent in response to increasing use of force by the State authorities. The community alleges that the State government has used deceit, force, and threats to get consent for the feasibility study. Abhinay Lakshman reports on the resistance

articles.title: Trump humbled at home, but what next abroad?
articles.description: A sweeping Democratic victory in the US midterms has raised questions about public support for Trump’s policies on immigration, the economy and foreign affairs. The consequences of the outcome for foreign policy and India are still uncertain.

articles.title: U.S. FBI and regulators issue warning about cyber-attacks targeting industrial refrigerators
articles.description: The U.S. regulators warned organisations about “ongoing cyber threat activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems,” shortly after these hacks led to huge amounts of food waste across European supermarkets

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 nears historic milestone: It will soon be one light-day away from Earth
articles.description: Nearly 5 decades after its launch, NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching a historic one-light-day milestone, putting it more than 16 billion miles from Earth. As the spacecraft moves deeper into space, engineers are battling declining power, ageing equipment and unexpected communication disruptions.

articles.title: Martian meteorite found in Sahara is 4.1 billion years old: What NASA-funded scientists discovered
articles.description: The meteorite was named after the Teghaza salt plain in Mali, where it was discovered. It is among roughly 435 Martian meteorites identified on Earth and is considered one of the three most ancient samples of the Red Planet found so far.

articles.title: ISRO launches NVS-03 satellite: Why was the mission crucial? How India's GPS alternative NavIC boosts strategic autonomy
articles.description: ISRO's successful launch of NVS-03 aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket has restored India's NavIC navigation system to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites. Why is the mission crucial for India's strategic autonomy, and how could NavIC reduce dependence on foreign navigation systems?

articles.title: ISRO's GSLV-F18 launches NVS-03 satellite carrying indigenous Rubidium atomic clock
articles.description: ISRO successfully launched the 2,232-kg NVS-03 navigation satellite aboard a GSLV rocket from Sriharikota. Equipped with indigenous and procured atomic clocks, NVS-03 will strengthen NavIC, adding L1-band signals to its services across India and about 1,500 km beyond.

articles.description: Retatrutide is widely expected to fuel Lilly's next wave of growth following the success of its Zepbound and Mounjaro.

articles.description: ISRO is all set to launch the much-awaited navigation satellite NVS-03 aboard a GSLV rocket on Friday.

articles.title: Meet Satyendra Nath Bose, the Indian physicist whose work transformed quantum physics and inspired the name ‘bosons’
articles.description: Satyendra Nath Bose was an Indian physicist whose groundbreaking work transformed quantum physics. In 1924, he sent a paper to Albert Einstein, who recognised its importance and helped publish it. His research laid the foundation for Bose-Einstein statistics and inspired the term ‘bosons’.

articles.title: Meet Gunisha Kaur, the 16-year-old eco-hero creating inclusive gardens for pollinators and children across Indian cities
articles.description: Sixteen-year-old Gunisha Kaur from Ludhiana has won third place at the 2026 International Young Eco-Hero Awards. Her Buzzing Blooms initiative has created more than 20 pollinator gardens, recording a 155% rise in species richness.

articles.description: A powerful solar eruption recorded on 8 October could trigger a moderate geomagnetic storm on 11 October, NOAA has warned. The event may brighten auroras but could also affect satellite signals, radio communications, navigation systems and power networks.

articles.description: The ICMR is seeking pharmaceutical partners to commercialize a novel liquid formulation that reduces infant brain toxins by 85%, offering an easy, low-cost alternative to phototherapy and blood transfusions.

articles.description: Conditioning children “from the very beginning” to rely on medication rather than shifting their dietary and exercise habits could result in substantially higher healthcare costs over their lifetimes, WHO's head of nutrition said.&nbsp;

articles.title: Dry eye is not just about screens: Lesser-known factors that can affect eye health
articles.description: With World Sight Day on 8 October, eye care experts tell LiveMint that dry eye can have several causes beyond prolonged screen use. They urge people to recognize broader risk factors and seek appropriate eye treatment, rather than attributing persistent symptoms solely to screen time.

articles.title: Michigan farm used this 10.22-kg rock as a doorstop for decades. It was a meteorite
articles.description: A 10.22-kg rock used as a barn doorstop on a Michigan farm for decades has been confirmed as an iron meteorite from the IIIAB group. Found after a reported 1939 fall near Edmore, the rock was identified by Central Michigan University and later studied by the Smithsonian Institution.

articles.description: The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) has been developed by DronAgni Combat Drones Pvt Ltd, a group company of AKSI Aerospace. The company describes Agni Kalash as a long-range platform designed for precision strike missions.

articles.description: Francis Halzen receives the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his pivotal contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the identification of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, leveraging South Pole ice to monitor cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann Georg Nagel awarded Nobel Medicine Prize: Who are they? Know their research fields
